source.title: The sharp, the flat and the shallow: Can weakly interacting agents learn to escape bad minima?
source.authors: Nikolas Kantas; P. Parpas; G. Pavliotis

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a small classification experiment comparing SGLD and a homogenized variant on test accuracy, bearing on generalization, but it does not test the random-label memorization claim or most listed conditions.
record.gate_note: The co-centric ellipse experiment reports similar loss and test accuracy for SGLD and HOM-SGLD and different behavior outside the observed data range. Toy optimization results and cited prior work do not report the claim's train-test generalization gap and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper assumes flat minima are desirable and develops smoothing algorithms, reporting optimization performance and qualitative classification results. It does not test any of V1–V8: in particular, it measures neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that interacting agents and averaging offer promising loss smoothing and optimization improvements, while practical machine-learning benefits remain unclear. The ellipse example suggests possible robustness benefits but also dependence on the stability of the algorithm and model.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and illustrates SGLD variants with interacting agents and homogenization; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization experiments or the claim's listed interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The classification behavior changes with discretization: HOM-SGLD performs less well with explicit Euler than with Verlet; both methods have similar test accuracy in the reported Verlet comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: SGLD and HOM-SGLD attain similar reported loss and test accuracy on the ellipse task; HOM-SGLD produces sensible classifications over a broader input range, but eventually also exhibits anomalous extrapolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Homogenization can change extrapolation behavior despite similar held-out accuracy on this synthetic classification task.

fits_no_version.finding: HOM-SGLD classification deteriorates when the neural network is constructed using explicit Euler instead of Verlet with the same step size and other parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The qualitative classification benefit depends on the discretization used to construct the neural network.

record.problems: The only classification comparison is a simple co-centric ellipse task; numeric test accuracy and uncertainty are not reported. The authors characterize results as preliminary and qualitative, and report sensitivity to discretization. The reported out-of-range behavior does not measure the claim's same-distribution train-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: Toy optimization traces and distance-to-minimum comparisons in Section 6.1 concern global optimization rather than the claim's generalization gap. No other same-distribution classification result with an explicit outcome is separately reported.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects on held-out error and their dependence on data size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: General discussion of flat minima and cited reparameterization objections do not constitute a test of V7's specific magnitude-aware measure. Similar test accuracy between two smoothing methods also does not establish or refute a sharpness–generalization relationship.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance coexistence; random-label test chance; named architectures and recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning or regularization variants.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation of large-batch recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparison with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the co-centric ellipse classification problem; test accuracy compared with HOM-SGLD.
rows.note: This small experiment does not report a numeric accuracy or the train-test gap.
rows.check: The reported similarity in test accuracy is accurate, but this is a comparator in the study's own method evaluation, not evidence for any listed version. No numerical accuracy is reported.

rows.subject: HOM-SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the co-centric ellipse classification problem; test accuracy compared with SGLD.
rows.note: Authors report similar loss and test accuracy but give no numeric values.
rows.check: The reported similarity in test accuracy is accurate, but this evaluates the proposed method against SGLD and does not test any listed version. No numerical accuracy is reported.

rows.subject: SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Compared classification behavior outside the original data range after training.
rows.measure: classification probability behavior outside observed range
rows.value: strange behavior outside the original range, including at the bottom of the plotted domain
rows.note: This is out-of-distribution behavior, explicitly outside the claim's scope.
rows.check: This qualitative extrapolation result measures none of the listed versions; it belongs under fits_no_version rather than claim-evidence rows.

rows.subject: HOM-SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Compared classification behavior outside the original data range after training.
rows.value: solution valid in a broader range, but eventually exhibits similar behavior to SGLD
rows.note: This result concerns behavior outside the training data range, not same-distribution generalization.
rows.check: The broader valid input range and eventual anomalous behavior are accurately described, but measure none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: HOM-SGLD
rows.operation_detail: Trained using the explicit Euler scheme instead of Verlet discretization.
rows.value: no longer performs as well as before
rows.note: Authors say other algorithms are even worse in this case; no same-distribution test metric is given.
rows.check: Explicit Euler replaces Verlet in constructing the discretized neural network, not explicitly in discretizing the HOM-SGLD optimizer. The text does not separately establish that the Euler network retains 128 layers and 774 parameters. This qualitative model-discretization comparison tests no listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
